Demo objective: clear chapter → section → chunk boundaries, focused concepts, and explicit prerequisite statements
make this document suitable for testing Learnify's Knowledge Map pipeline.
IES Demo Material • Page 2

Chunk 1 — What Is an Embedded System?
An embedded system is a computing system designed to perform a dedicated function inside a larger product. It
combines hardware and software and operates under constraints such as timing, memory, power, cost and reliability.
Concepts: Embedded System; Dedicated Function; Hardware–Software Integration; Resource Constraints.
Chunk 2 — Real-Time Behavior
A real-time system must respond to events within defined timing constraints. Hard real-time systems have deadlines
whose violation can cause failure, while soft real-time systems tolerate occasional deadline misses.
Concepts: Real-Time System; Deadline; Hard Real-Time; Soft Real-Time.

Chunk 3 — Microcontroller Basics
A microcontroller integrates a processor core, memory, timers and peripheral interfaces on one chip. It is optimized for
controlling physical devices and interacting with sensors and actuators.
Concepts: Microcontroller; Processor Core; Memory; Peripheral.
PREREQUISITE: Understanding embedded systems is required before studying microcontroller architecture.
Chunk 4 — CPU, Memory and Peripherals
The CPU executes instructions, memory stores program code and data, and peripherals provide specialized functions
such as timers, serial communication, analog conversion and digital input/output.
Concepts: CPU; Program Memory; Data Memory; Peripheral Interface.
PREREQUISITE: Microcontroller basics are required before studying CPU, memory and peripheral relationships.
IES Demo Material • Page 3

Chunk 5 — GPIO Fundamentals
GPIO pins allow a microcontroller to read digital signals and control external devices. A pin can be configured as an
input to read a switch or as an output to drive an LED.
Concepts: GPIO; Digital Input; Digital Output; Pin Configuration.
Chunk 6 — Pull-Up and Pull-Down Resistors
A floating digital input can produce unpredictable readings. Pull-up and pull-down resistors establish a default logic
level until an external device changes the state.
Concepts: Floating Input; Pull-Up; Pull-Down; Logic Level.
PREREQUISITE: GPIO fundamentals are required before understanding pull-up and pull-down configuration.

Chunk 7 — Sensors and Physical Signals
A sensor converts a physical quantity such as temperature, light, pressure or motion into an electrical signal that a
controller can measure.
Concepts: Sensor; Physical Quantity; Electrical Signal; Measurement.
Chunk 8 — Analog-to-Digital Conversion
An ADC maps a continuous electrical signal to a discrete numerical representation. Resolution determines how finely
the input range can be represented.
Concepts: ADC; Analog Signal; Digital Representation; Resolution.
PREREQUISITE: Sensors and electrical signals are required before studying ADC-based measurement.

Chunk 9 — Interrupt Concept
An interrupt temporarily transfers processor control to an interrupt service routine when an event requires immediate
attention. Normal execution resumes after the routine completes.
Concepts: Interrupt; Interrupt Service Routine; Event; Processor Context.
PREREQUISITE: Basic processor execution is required before understanding interrupt handling.
Chunk 10 — Polling Versus Interrupts
Polling repeatedly checks whether an event has occurred. Interrupt-driven design allows hardware to notify the
processor when an event occurs, improving responsiveness.
Concepts: Polling; Interrupt-Driven Design; Responsiveness; Event Handling.
PREREQUISITE: GPIO event handling provides a foundation for comparing polling with interrupts.
IES Demo Material • Page 4

Chunk 11 — UART Communication
UART provides asynchronous serial communication using transmit and receive lines. Data is commonly framed with
start and stop bits and transferred at a configured baud rate.
Concepts: UART; Serial Communication; Baud Rate; Data Frame.
PREREQUISITE: GPIO and digital signaling provide the foundation for UART.
Chunk 12 — I2C Communication
I2C is a synchronous bus using clock and data lines and supporting multiple addressed devices. A controller can
communicate with sensors and other peripherals over the shared bus.
Concepts: I2C; Synchronous Bus; Addressing; Controller; Peripheral.
PREREQUISITE: Digital signaling and addressing are required before studying I2C.

Chunk 13 — Why Use an RTOS?
A real-time operating system provides scheduling and synchronization mechanisms for applications with multiple
concurrent activities and timing requirements.
Concepts: RTOS; Scheduling; Concurrency; Timing Requirement.
PREREQUISITE: Real-time behavior and timing constraints are required before studying RTOS.
Chunk 14 — Tasks and Scheduling
An RTOS divides application behavior into tasks. A scheduler decides which task executes, often according to priority
and timing requirements.
Concepts: Task; Scheduler; Priority; Context Switch.
PREREQUISITE: RTOS fundamentals are required before studying task scheduling.

Chunk 15 — Shared Resources
Concurrent tasks may access the same data or hardware resource. Without coordination, interleaving operations can
create inconsistent results and race conditions.
Concepts: Shared Resource; Concurrency; Race Condition.
PREREQUISITE: Tasks and concurrency are required before analyzing shared-resource problems.
Chunk 16 — Mutexes and Semaphores
A mutex provides controlled exclusive access to a shared resource. A semaphore can coordinate events or control
access to a limited number of resources.
Concepts: Mutex; Semaphore; Mutual Exclusion; Synchronization.
PREREQUISITE: Shared-resource problems must be understood before selecting mutexes or semaphores.
IES Demo Material • Page 5

Chunk 17 — IoT Architecture
An IoT system connects physical devices to networks and software services. A typical architecture contains sensing,
local processing, communication, data storage and application layers.
Concepts: IoT; Edge Device; Network; Cloud Service; Data Pipeline.
PREREQUISITE: Embedded sensing and communication are required before designing an IoT architecture.
Chunk 18 — Telemetry Pipeline
Telemetry is the collection and transmission of measurements from an embedded device. A reliable pipeline validates
readings, attaches timestamps, transmits data and stores measurements.
Concepts: Telemetry; Timestamp; Data Validation; Data Transmission; Storage.
PREREQUISITE: Sensors, ADC and communication interfaces are required before designing a telemetry pipeline.

Chunk 19 — Smart Temperature Monitor
A smart temperature monitor reads a sensor through an ADC, periodically samples the value using a scheduled task,
transmits measurements using a communication interface and stores telemetry for later analysis.
Concepts: Temperature Monitoring; Sampling; ADC; Scheduled Task; Communication; Telemetry.
PREREQUISITE: Sensor measurement, ADC, task scheduling, communication and telemetry are required for the
integrated design.
Chunk 20 — System Design Review
A complete embedded solution connects requirements, hardware interfaces, software tasks, timing behavior and data
flow. Designers verify each dependency before integrating the system.
Concepts: System Integration; Requirements; Hardware Interface; Software Task; Data Flow.
PREREQUISITE: The integrated design depends on foundations from Chapters 1–4.
